facts.t: Appears in 2.02% of the 23,711 paintings in our archive (479 paintings, as photographed; the within-painting lens finds it in 240).
In our 23,711-painting archive it is more common than 72% of the named colors.
Peaks in the 1900s: found in 1.9% of the 1,668 paintings we have from then (32 paintings). Against the same museums' baseline that is 1.8x the expected rate.
Inside a painting it most often plays a hidden color (38% of the 240 paintings, by lightness rank within each painting, so varnish cannot fake it).
Most devoted painter: Paul Cezanne, in 8 of 50 works here (6.5x the baseline of the museums those works come from; as photographed 5.0x; n=8).

First seen in our archive in 1375 (aic-59843); the third-earliest painting is 1435, and the latest 1950 (388 dated paintings, at least 2% of the canvas, as photographed). The archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first.
Shares canvases with Deep Slate-Olive and Artichoke Green more than chance (lift 9.3 and 6.4; n=34 and 30).
In printed English the word peaks in the 2000s and rose fastest in the 1920s (Google Books, all senses of the word, so a color name that is also an object or a place can mislead).
